# Dotty Hargreave

## Description
Short, square, fifties, with forearms like hams and a voice that reaches the loft
through two floors. Permanently mid-sentence. Wears a paper crown over her cap because
her cousins put it there and she has decided it suits her.

## Personality & motivation
Warm, practical, nosy, and running a full inn in a blizzard on a festival day, so busy
to the point of fury. She wants the sausage cart to arrive (it does not), the ale to
last (it does), and the goose-herder to stop frightening the guests. She would never
turn out a traveller in snow. She will absolutely charge them for a second breakfast.

## Knowledge & secrets
- Freely shares: everything about everyone in Bellwether; the programme; that Wil "has been odd since Midwinter, which, yes, is today, don't ask me, he's been odd since breakfast"; that the castle "has been up there since the morning, we're all very proud"; that the cart from the monastery is late "again" and she will have words with the Abbot; the post "comes up through the hearth hatch, don't feed them, they unionise"; Pim is "nobody's, so he's mine, so he's yours if he's useful, and he is"
- Needs persuasion (DC 12): the chalk tally on the loft beam has been there "as long as I can remember, which this morning is about an hour"; she has a feeling about the loft she does not like and sleeps in the kitchen
- Never: she does not know anything secret. She is hollow in the ordinary way, and kind

(none yet)

- 14:00–16:00 → sleeping-marmot/common-room (behind the bar)
